title: How to build a simple CRM without code | 50agents
description: Build a simple CRM without code: ten fields, five stages, a next follow-up date on every open lead and a daily list of who to contact.
h1: How to build a simple CRM without code
answer: Make one list of leads with about ten fields, five stages, and a next follow-up date on every open lead.
Sort by that date each morning, and get new leads in from email and forms without typing.

root.q: How many people work the same leads?

then.q: Do leads arrive faster than you can type them in?

then.why: Add the fields below, dropdowns for Stage and Source, and a Follow up view sorted by date.

then.answer: A no-code app that captures and reminds
then.why: It adds leads from your inbox and puts today's follow-ups in front of you, so nothing depends on your memory.
Two people in one sheet overwrite each other with no history. An app gives each lead one record and a change log.
Email tracking, sequences and reporting across reps are what full CRMs are built for.

body.p: Make Stage and Source dropdowns, not free text, so they sort and count. You need three views: Follow up (open leads, soonest date first, every morning), Pipeline (a board by stage, weekly) and All leads (searchable, when someone calls).

steps.title: Make the list with these fields
steps.body: In a sheet, one tab with one row per lead. In a no-code app, one table.

steps.title: Add the three views
steps.body: A sorted tab or filter view for Follow up; a board for Pipeline if your tool has one.

steps.title: Bring in what you have
steps.body: Paste last quarter's leads from email and your notes. Fill Stage and Next follow-up for every open one.

steps.title: Decide how new leads get in
steps.body: Form entries, enquiry emails, referrals: each needs a route into the list.

note.text: Without a route in, the CRM goes stale within a month. Automate capture, or set ten minutes a day to add leads.

steps.title: Set the follow-up rule
steps.body: Each time you contact a lead, set Last contact to today and Next follow-up to a date. No open lead without a date.

note.text: Make Next follow-up required for every open stage. Leads with no date never show up in Follow up.

steps.title: Review the pipeline weekly
steps.body: Move dead leads to Lost. A pipeline full of ghosts hides the real ones.

captain.line: Captain builds this CRM with an AI agent that reads your email each weekday, adds new people asking to buy, and drafts follow-ups for your approval.

wrong.title: Duplicate leads
wrong.body: The same person arrives from a form and an email. Use email as the key and search before adding.

wrong.title: Stages nobody agrees on
wrong.body: "Qualified" means three things to three people. Keep five plain stages and write one line on what each means.

wrong.title: Two people, one sheet
wrong.body: Edits overwrite each other and there is no history. Move to an app with records and a change log.

wrong.title: A drafted follow-up misreads the lead
wrong.body: An AI agent can mistake a supplier for a buyer. Approve each draft before it goes, and correct the stage when it is wrong.

faqs.q: Can Google Sheets be a CRM?
faqs.a: Yes, for one person or a small team with a few dozen open leads. Add the fields above, dropdowns for stage and source, and a Follow up view sorted by date.

faqs.q: What columns should a simple CRM have?
faqs.a: Name, email, phone, company, source, stage, deal size, last contact, next follow-up and notes. Add more only when you make a decision with them.

faqs.q: When should I move to a real CRM?
faqs.a: When several people work the same leads, when you need email tracking and sequences, or when follow-ups keep slipping despite the sheet.
